arc.hook: Most failed AI pilots do not die because the model was bad. They die after the demo, when the product has to survive shift changes, inbox overload, unclear ownership, and the thousand small frictions of real clinical operations.
arc.setup: The typical pilot is scoped around model performance and stakeholder excitement. A team proves the alert can fire or the summary can generate, but nobody redesigns the surrounding workflow: who sees it, when they act, what they stop doing, and how the result is measured.
arc.turn: The better question is not whether the demo works. It is who behaves differently on Tuesday morning because this AI exists, and whether that behavior is specific enough to train, staff, escalate, and audit without a product manager standing in the room.
arc.payoff: Before approving a pilot, force four operational answers into the plan: one accountable owner, one clear trigger, one escalation path when confidence is low, and one measurement window tied to a real workflow metric. If any of those are vague, the pilot is not ready.
arc.cta: Pick one active AI pilot this week and score it against those four fields. If the owner, trigger, escalation path, or measurement window cannot be named in one sentence each, pause the expansion work and repair the operating model first.

timeline.voiceover: Most failed AI pilots do not die because the model was bad.
timeline.visual: Fast stack of abandoned pilot cards collapsing into a clean operations board.
timeline.on_screen_text: The pilot was not the product.

timeline.voiceover: They die because the workflow never changed. The alert fires, the team nods, and then everyone keeps doing the old process.
timeline.visual: Split screen: shiny demo on the left, unchanged clinic queue on the right.

timeline.voiceover: Before approving a pilot, ask four questions. Who owns the action? What triggers it? Where does escalation go? When do we measure the change?
timeline.visual: Four checklist blocks animate in one by one.

timeline.voiceover: If those answers are vague, you do not have an AI implementation. You have a science fair project with a budget code.
timeline.visual: Budget stamp turns into a project roadmap with accountable names.

timeline.voiceover: Take one active pilot and score it against those four fields this week.
timeline.visual: Checklist locks into a shareable scorecard.
